plan.groundTruth:
**What this app is today.** `reep-dashboard` is a Next 16 / React 19 / MUI 9 / Prisma 6 (Postgres) app for "BGSCET MBA — REEP Tracking Dashboard" (package.json description). It has three role areas under `src/app` — `student/` (page, courses, certifications, time-log, uploads, profile, resume, assistant), `mentor/` ((overview), student, student/[id], alerts, reports, uploads, settings, assistant), `director/` — plus `login/` and `api/` (activity, activity/bulk, alerts/scan, agent, auth/logout, checkin, export/*, resume/generate, sync, uploads, uploads/[id], uploads/[id]/review). Auth is a jose JWT cookie (`src/lib/auth.ts`) with `middleware.ts` matching only `['/student/:path*','/mentor/:path*','/director/:path*']` and redirecting cookie-less requests to `/login`. Every account today is created by `prisma/seed.ts` (927 lines). Domain logic lives in pure, `server-only`-free modules (`activity-rules.ts`, `llm-parse.ts`, `analytics.ts`, `progress.ts`, `reep.ts`, `rules.ts`, `mentor-scope.ts`) with vitest tests; `server-only` modules (`queries.ts`, `auth.ts`, `uploads.ts`, `upload-access.ts`, `ai/llm.ts`, …) are stubbed in tests via `vitest.config.mts`. Migrations: 4, ending at `20260805061500_lab_session_created_at`.

**How much of the spec it already satisfies: roughly 15%, and two of those are load-bearing-broken.**

Already present and reusable: shared login (`src/app/login/`) covers spec 6 in substance; mentee list + drill-through exists (`src/app/mentor/student/page.tsx`, `mentee-grid.tsx`, `student/[id]/page.tsx`) for spec 7; `MentorNote` with `createdAt` and a write path (`src/app/mentor/student/[id]/actions.ts`) covers most of spec 8; `StudentProfile.linkedinUrl` exists (spec 1); `UploadKind.PROFILE_PHOTO` / `RESUME` / `CERTIFICATE_PROOF` plus a hardened storage layer (`src/lib/uploads.ts`: generated UUID filenames, `safeExtension`, `resolveInsideRoot`) and a mentor review flow (`UploadStatus`, `src/app/api/uploads/[id]/review/route.ts`, `src/app/mentor/uploads/review-panel.tsx`) exist; the resume builder (`Resume.jobDescription`, `src/lib/ai/resume.ts`, `src/app/api/resume/generate/route.ts`, `src/app/student/resume/[id]`) is a near-fit for spec 2(d); attendance data (`AttendanceRecord`) and `Stage` back two tiles of spec 1; `exceljs` is already a dependency, so XLSX ingest needs no new package.

Confirmed absent — verified by reading `prisma/schema.prisma` end to end and grepping `src/`: **no** registration route or model, **no** profile approval status, **no** email verification, **no** domain allowlist, **no** CV parser, **no** VTU/marks model of any kind, **no** SWOC, **no** mock-attempt record, **no** login-day history (only `User.lastLoginAt`, a single overwritten timestamp), **no** normalised skill table (skills are `StudentProfile.skills Json`), **no** Job / JobApplication, **no** degree-level field anywhere, **no** mail capability (dependencies are @anthropic-ai/sdk, @emotion/*, @mui/*, @prisma/client, exceljs, jose, next, react, react-dom, zod), **no** scheduler (`npm start` is plain `next start -p 3100`; the only "cron" mention is an aspirational comment in `src/app/api/sync/route.ts`), **no** leaderboard route, **no** student-to-student read path (`visibleStudentWhere` pins a STUDENT to `{ id: selfStudentId }`), and **no** leave model.

Two existing-code hazards the plan must fix before building on them, both verified: (a) `src/app/mentor/student/[id]/page.tsx:143` reads `if (session.mentorId && data.student.mentorId !== session.mentorId) notFound();` — the exact anti-pattern `src/lib/mentor-scope.ts` was written to eliminate; a MENTOR with no `Mentor` row short-circuits to false and reads *any* student's full detail, and the same test at `actions.ts:48` and `:221` lets that account *write* notes on any student. Same shape at `mentor/student/page.tsx:36`, `mentor/reports/page.tsx:120/140/146`, `mentor/reports/export/route.ts:41`, `api/alerts/scan/route.ts:32`. (b) `src/lib/ai/resume.ts:249` enters the Anthropic path on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` alone with no `studentDataEgressAllowed()` check, and `resumeWriterBlocked()` returns false in that configuration — so the banner says nothing while the student's name, USN, marks and attendance go to api.anthropic.com. Spec 2(d) (per-job CV) would inherit both.

Everything else in the spec is net-new, and the plan below sequences it so no page phase depends on a model that has not landed.

conflicts.conflict: "Exactly 5 activities" for the student time sheet vs. a live 15-value ActivityType enum that the whole analytics engine is keyed to. Collapsing the enum destroys the mocks-taken chart the SAME spec asks for (spec 1 lists GD/Interview/Aptitude, currently the only mock signal is MOCK_INTERVIEW/APTITUDE_PREP), plus focus quality, the LOW_FOCUS_QUALITY alert rule, pace, and every export.
conflicts.spec: Spec 5: "Student time sheet: must be very easy to fill. Exactly 5 activities: sleeping, engaged in leisure, engaged in lectures, engaged in coursework, engaged in skilling."
conflicts.existing: prisma/schema.prisma:126 enum ActivityType has 15 members; prisma/schema.prisma:355 LabSession.activity is non-null with @default(ONLINE_COURSE). Consumers: src/lib/activity-rules.ts, src/lib/analytics.ts, src/lib/ai/agent/tools.ts, src/app/api/activity/route.ts, src/app/api/activity/bulk/route.ts, src/app/student/time-log/*, src/lib/export/collect.ts, scripts/verify-formulas.ts, prisma/seed.ts, and the assertions in src/lib/activity-rules.test.ts and src/lib/analytics.test.ts.
conflicts.recommendation: Do NOT mutate ActivityType. Add a NEW enum `DayActivity { SLEEPING, LEISURE, LECTURES, COURSEWORK, SKILLING }` and a NEW model `TimeSheetEntry(studentId, day @db.Date, activity DayActivity, minutes Int)` with @@unique([studentId, day, activity]). The spec clause is scoped to the student time sheet, and a time sheet whose picker offers exactly five buttons satisfies it literally. `/student/time-log` becomes that five-bucket sheet as its default view; the existing course-linked session log moves to `/student/time-log/sessions` (unchanged semantics, still the source of pace/focus/cert progress). Nothing is dropped and nothing is reinterpreted. Sleeping and leisure minutes are excluded from every learning aggregate by construction because they live in a different table.

conflicts.conflict: The mocks-taken chart cannot be derived from time-log data at all, whichever way the enum question is resolved. APTITUDE_PREP is preparation time, not a test taken with a score, and there is no GD value.

conflicts.spec: Spec 4: "Leaderboards page: several different leaderboards — by certificate uploads, by skills, by VTU results, by login streak, by mocks taken."

conflicts.conflict: "Auto-approve if within specified domains" makes an unverified email claim into a trust decision. Combined with the leaderboards (spec 4), a stranger typing an @bgscet.ac.in address they do not control would get a STUDENT session that reads other students' data.

openQuestions.question: "Auto-approve the profile if within specified domains" — does "domains" mean the applicant's email domain (e.g. @bgscet.ac.in), or their academic/skill domain (branch, programme, discipline)?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: It decides the shape of RegistrationRule and of the whole auto-approve branch. Guessing wrong means rebuilding the rule engine, the review queue filters and the director settings screen. Nothing in the repo hints either way — there is no allowlist config anywhere.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Implement BOTH as an AND: a verified email-domain allowlist AND a declared programme/branch allowlist, each editable by a director in a `RegistrationRule` table, each independently disableable. An applicant passing both is auto-approved; anything else goes to review. This satisfies either reading without a rewrite.

openQuestions.question: Is Undergraduate onboarding actually in scope for this iteration, or only UG/PG *separation* on the jobs page?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: Full UG support means USN parsing, cohort structure, semester counts (8 vs 4), and the REEP Stage definitions all need review — that is a programme-modelling exercise, not a filter. Doing it unasked burns weeks; skipping it silently ships a UG tab with nothing in it.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Model DegreeLevel on Cohort/Student/Job and implement real filtering plus UG-capable registration, but do NOT redesign Stage, the course catalogue, or semester logic for UG. Flag in the director UI that UG cohorts have no REEP curriculum loaded.

openQuestions.question: In the SWOC chart's "three sources: placement, mentor, PM" — who are "placement" and "PM" in the role model? Are they new staff accounts, or existing directors wearing a hat?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: prisma/schema.prisma enum Role is only STUDENT|MENTOR|DIRECTOR|ADMIN, and requireMentor() admits MENTOR/DIRECTOR/ADMIN. Adding Role values changes HOME_FOR_ROLE (a Record<Role,string>), mentorScope's PROGRAMME_WIDE list and every role switch — cheap to do now, expensive to retrofit after four more screens exist.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Add `PLACEMENT` and `PM` to enum Role, map both to '/mentor' in HOME_FOR_ROLE, and explicitly keep them OUT of mentorScope()'s PROGRAMME_WIDE list (they are not mentors and get `{ kind: 'none' }` for mentee screens). Grant them programme-wide SWOC authorship only, through a separate `swocAuthorScope()`. SwocEntry.source is a hard three-value enum regardless of who typed it.

openQuestions.question: Where do VTU marks come from — a director/office bulk upload, per-student manual entry by staff, or a scrape of the VTU results portal?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: Both the VTU marks chart (spec 1) and the VTU leaderboard (spec 4) are undeliverable without a real source. A scrape is a different project with its own legal and reliability profile.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Director-facing XLSX/CSV upload (exceljs is already a dependency, so no new package) with a documented column format, plus per-student manual correction. No scraping. A dry-run preview before commit, and re-import is idempotent on (studentId, semester, subjectCode).

openQuestions.question: What exactly is "the jobs list sheet"? A Google Sheet the placement office maintains, an XLSX someone emails around, or a form the office fills in the dashboard?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: A Google Sheet means a googleapis dependency, a service account and a shared-credential story; an uploaded file means none of that. This decides Phase 7's first three tasks and is a product decision, not an implementation detail.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: XLSX/CSV upload by a director or placement user at /director/jobs, parsed with exceljs, plus an authenticated `/api/jobs/import/run` for an external scheduler. Dedupe key: (sourceRef ?? normalised(company + title + applyUrl)). If it turns out to be a Google Sheet, only the fetch step changes — the parser takes rows, not a file.

openQuestions.question: May a student see another student's raw VTU marks on the leaderboard, and may students opt out of appearing?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: Spec 4 demands the board; publishing exam performance cohort-wide is a privacy decision the spec does not explicitly authorise and that no code in this repo currently permits. Building it the naive way and retracting it later means the data has already been shown.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Show display name + rank + a coarse band (e.g. 'First Class'), never the raw mark or USN, and only within the viewer's own cohort. The viewer always sees their own exact figure. A `leaderboardOptOut` toggle on the profile removes the student from all boards. Same rule for the certificate-uploads board (count only, no titles).

openQuestions.question: Must the five time-sheet buckets total 24 hours for a day, and is that a hard block or a warning?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: 'Sleeping' as a bucket strongly implies whole-day accounting, and the validation rule changes the entire interaction design of the sheet — which the spec explicitly grades ('must be very easy to fill').
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Soft-require: block a total above 24h, warn (do not block) below it, and show remaining hours live. Save is allowed at any total so the sheet is never a wall.

openQuestions.question: Does the five-bucket time sheet replace the existing per-course session log the student fills at /student/time-log, or sit alongside it?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: Course-linked session hours drive pace status, focus quality, the LOW_FOCUS_QUALITY alert and cert progress (src/lib/progress.ts, src/lib/analytics.ts). Removing the student's ability to log them would quietly hollow out the mentor screens.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Alongside. The five-bucket sheet becomes the default view at /student/time-log; the existing session log moves to /student/time-log/sessions with unchanged semantics and a link between them. No existing data is migrated or reinterpreted.

openQuestions.question: Who reviews a registration from an applicant who has no mentor yet, and who are the first and second approvers for a mentor's leave request?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: mentorScope() has no answer for an applicant with no mentorId, and the Mentor model has no reporting-line field at all — so 'second approver' has no source. Both flows stall on this.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Registrations: DIRECTOR and ADMIN only (mentors see nothing until assignment). Leave: `firstApproverUserId` becomes a configurable field on the Mentor record (director-set, defaults to the cohort's director); the second approver is any DIRECTOR. Second approver sees the request only after the first has approved; a rejection at either stage ends it.

openQuestions.question: Does an unverified certificate-backed skill claim count toward badges, the skills leaderboard and the job match percentage?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: If yes, all three are trivially gamed by uploading any file. If no, a student's genuine skills are invisible until a mentor gets to them, which changes the perceived value of the whole skilling page.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Only VERIFIED claims light a badge, score on the leaderboard, or count in the match percentage. Pending claims show to the student as 'awaiting verification' and to their mentor in the existing /mentor/uploads review queue.

openQuestions.question: Which mail transport and which sender identity for the weekly job alert and the registration verification email?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: There is no mail capability at all in this repo (no nodemailer/resend/sendgrid, no MAIL_* keys in .env.example). Institutional mail usually needs an authorised relay or a verified sending domain — that is a request to the college's IT, with lead time.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: nodemailer over SMTP, configured by MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PORT/MAIL_USER/MAIL_PASS/MAIL_FROM in .env.example, with a console transport as the automatic dev default so nothing blocks on credentials. Every send is recorded so a re-run cannot double-send.

openQuestions.question: Is it acceptable for a prospective student's CV (name, phone, address) to be sent to a remote model for auto-fill, or must parsing stay on the machine?
openQuestions.whyItBlocks: AGENTS.md makes this an explicit project rule, and LLM_BASE_URL may legitimately point at OpenRouter/Groq/Gemini. If remote is forbidden, CV auto-fill must be deterministic-first and the UX must say what it could not extract.
openQuestions.defaultIfUnanswered: Treat a CV as student data: route the parse through studentDataEgressAllowed() exactly as generateResume does. When the gate refuses, fall back to deterministic regex/heading extraction and tell the applicant which fields to fill in by hand. Never silently send.

phases.name: Phase 0 — Safety prerequisites (must land before any new surface)

Every one of these is a blocker raised by the safety review and verified against the repo. Doing them first means the new features inherit correct behaviour instead of propagating the bug; doing them later means auditing twice as much surface.

plan.verification:
**Per-phase exit gate (every phase, non-negotiable).** `npm run db:reset && npm run typecheck && npm run test` must all pass before the phase is considered done. `db:reset` is `prisma migrate reset --force --skip-seed && npm run db:seed`, so any schema change that is not accompanied by a matching prisma/seed.ts update fails here rather than three phases later — this is why every Phase 1 task carries its seed edit inside the task. `npm run lint` and `npm run build` additionally run at the end of each phase that adds a route, because a client/server boundary mistake (importing a `server-only` module into a client component) is a build error, not a test failure.

**Phase 0 (safety).** Unit-level: new cases in src/lib/mentor-scope.test.ts and test/confirmed-defects.test.ts assert a MENTOR session with `mentorId: undefined` yields zero students from every converted call site and that menteeWhere() never returns `{}` for a MENTOR; a new src/lib/ai/agent/scope.test.ts asserts the same for the assistant; src/lib/ai/egress.test.ts gains a case proving the Anthropic path is refused when LLM_ALLOW_REMOTE_STUDENT_DATA is unset and that resumeWriterBlocked() reports true in that configuration; src/lib/upload-sniff.test.ts asserts a file declaring `image/png` with a `<svg` body is rejected. Manual: sign in as the seeded mentor account with its Mentor row deleted and confirm /mentor/student/<other-student-id> returns 404 and the note form refuses.

**Phase 1 (schema).** `npm run db:migrate` generates exactly one migration for the phase; `npm run db:reset` proves it applies to an empty database and that the seed populates every new model. Hand-check the generated SQL for the two backfills (MentorNote.meetingAt = createdAt, Cohort.degreeLevel = 'PG'). `npx prisma validate` and `npm run typecheck` catch the Record<Role, …> sites the Role enum change breaks (src/lib/auth.ts HOME_FOR_ROLE, src/lib/ai/agent/scope.ts SCOPE_BY_ROLE) — that failure is expected and is the forcing function.

**Phases 2-9 (features).** Every pure module lands with its own `*.test.ts` next to it, per the repo's existing convention (activity-rules.test.ts, analytics.test.ts, mentor-scope.test.ts, llm-parse.test.ts): registration/schema, registration/rules, registration/cv-map, registration/provision, skills/recommend (asserts exactly 5), leaderboard-scope (asserts the payload type carries no usn / raw mark / attendance %), leaderboard/boards (asserts five boards and stable tie-breaks), marks/parse, jobs/parse, jobs/match (including the empty-skills case), jobs/alert-copy, timesheet/rules (asserts exactly 5 activities and the 24h rule), streak, leave/rules, leave/scope, swoc/scope, mail/compose, rate-limit, upload-sniff.

Manual run-through per phase against the seeded database, using `npm run dev` (port 3100) and the seeded accounts: Phase 2 — register with a non-allowlisted address and confirm it lands in the review queue, register with an allowlisted address and confirm the verification mail is required before auto-approval (console transport prints the link), approve one and sign in as the created student. Phase 3 — upload a certificate, claim a skill, verify it as a mentor, watch the badge light. Phase 4 — import a marks sheet twice and confirm the second import creates nothing new. Phase 5 — load /student for a brand-new student with no data and confirm all eight tiles render empty states rather than crashing. Phase 6 — sign in as two students in the same cohort and confirm neither can see the other's raw marks in the network payload (check the RSC response, not just the DOM). Phase 7 — run `npm run jobs:weekly` twice and confirm MailLog prevents a second send. Phase 8 — fill a whole day on /student/time-log and time it; run `tsx scripts/verify-formulas.ts` to prove no learning aggregate moved. Phase 9 — submit a leave request, confirm the second approver cannot see it until the first has approved, and confirm a rejection at stage one ends it.

**Final acceptance (Phase 10).** `scripts/spec-acceptance.ts` prints one row per spec clause with the route/module satisfying it and the test proving it, and exits non-zero on any unchecked row. The three clauses most prone to silent under-delivery get dedicated assertions: SWOC renders three distinct sources, the mocks chart renders GD + Interview + Aptitude, and /student/leaderboards renders exactly five boards. Plus the existing whole-app smoke scripts: `tsx scripts/smoke.ts`, `tsx scripts/sanity-check.ts`, `tsx scripts/test-uploads.ts`, `tsx scripts/test-activity.ts` — and note that any NEW standalone script must import only `server-only`-free modules or it will die with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, per AGENTS.md.
